title: Apple Silicon genome aligner hillclimb
models: Claude Opus 5.5 in GitHub Copilot CLI for most of the work, with GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol on the first day
machines: M1 Pro (8P+2E cores, 32 GB) for the main measurements; a base M1 Mac mini (16 GB) and GitHub's virtual M1 runners (7 GiB) for small Macs
data: hs38 (GRCh38 without ALTs) with the first 5M HG002 30x NovaSeq read pairs, 9 threads, unless noted
rule: Every build had to write byte-identical alignments to its upstream release (only the @PG line differs), checked by hashing the SAM records.

climbs.note: Exact replacements for upstream steps; the 0.8.0 and 0.9.0 rows are each from rounds interleaved with the version before.

steps.what: 16 interleaved suffix-array walks, batched 8-bit mate rescue, pointer sort, NEON unpacking (−32.8%)

climbs.note: Peak memory fell from 16.9 GiB to 11.5 GiB in 0.3.0 by not loading the 6.2 GB .0123 file.

steps.label: 0.1.0 --metal
steps.what: Seed extension batched on the GPU

steps.label: 0.2.0 --metal

minimap2.title: wgse-minimap2 (minimap2 2.31)

rows.reads: HiFi, 40k reads, index built from FASTA
ONT, 15k reads, index built from FASTA

notes: Index building went from 31.0 s to 7.4 s by sketching chromosomes on all threads with an exact warm-up.
0.2.0 --metal runs 85% of HiFi gap fills on the GPU at about 6.9 G cells/s, with 16 fibers per thread to keep batches full.

mem3.title: wgse-bwa-mem3 (bwa-mem3 0.16.0)
notes: bwa-mem3 already had NEON kernels, so the CPU build is upstream's code and no faster.
It then became WGS Extract's default stand-in for bwa and bwa-mem2 where memory allows: on a busy machine, 553 s → 175 s with bwa's exact records and 546 s → 75 s with bwa-mem2's.

energy.note: Package energy (CPU + GPU) with powermetrics on the 5M pairs, scaled to a 30x genome (×62). --metal draws more power but finishes so much sooner that it roughly halves the energy of both BWA tools.

smallMac.title: A base 16 GB M1 Mac mini
notes: A whole public HG002 35x genome went from BAM to personal report in 7.3 hours with default settings and the owner's apps open: realign 6 h 2 min (GPU-bound), SNP and indel calling 68 min, everything else under 4 min each.
Peak memory 8.4 GiB for one process (10.4 GiB summed), swap up to 4.8 GiB, about 166 GiB of free disk needed.
Accuracy against GIAB v4.2.1: SNPs 99.1% recall / 97.5% precision; indels 95.2% / 95.3%.
Measuring on this Mac fixed five defaults, including running wgse-bwa on Metal (about 4× faster than its CPU fallback) and calling SNPs per contig in parallel (849 s → 211 s).

hosted: On GitHub's virtual M1 runners (3 cores, 7 GiB), --metal was 4–5× faster than the CPU backends on chr1–3.
On the full human reference only wgse-bwa --metal reliably finished; the CPU runs and BWA-MEM2 (11–17 GiB) paged until they were stopped, which led to memory warnings in 0.4.1.
failed: Compiler tuning: Apple clang already targets apple-m1; ThinLTO, full LTO, PGO and mimalloc each changed BWA by about 1% or less.
A GPU chaining kernel for minimap2, and parking an OS thread per read while its gap fills waited for the GPU.
Scoring minimap2 chaining predecessors eight at a time with NEON: most scans stop early.
For bwa-mem3: mimalloc as malloc, LTO, PGO, -mcpu=apple-m1 and the denser suffix array (re-sa -u 2, slower at 14.5 GiB).
Rescuing bwa-mem3 mates on the GPU: no faster on the medium tier.
BWA-MEM2's own index can't be built on a Mac: it needs about 73 GB of RAM, so it was built on Linux.
